test: Seatbelt profile under the real kernel
an app in the workspace cannot be launched outside the sandbox
mayRuntimeSkip.reason: Skips at runtime (ctx.skip) when the probe app does not launch even unconfined, so the denial would prove nothing. Whether LaunchServices opens an unsigned bundle on a hosted runner is not established; a skip is recorded, a failure is not accepted.

test: Seatbelt profile under the real kernel
the login Keychain is unreachable through the security tool
mayRuntimeSkip.reason: Skips at runtime (ctx.skip) when the host user has no readable login Keychain item to compare against. A fresh hosted runner user is not expected to have one; a skip is recorded, a failure is not accepted.

test: Seatbelt profile under the real kernel
a direct TCP connection to this host's own non-loopback address is refused by the kernel
mayRuntimeSkip.reason: Skips at runtime (ctx.skip) when the host has no non-loopback IPv4 address, so there is no outside address of its own to compare against; the documentation-address leg proves the refusal on every host. A skip is recorded, a failure is not accepted.

test: Seatbelt profile under the real kernel
the installed Claude Code answers its handshake from inside the profile, and the provider observes it confined
notRequired.reason: Guarded by test.skipIf(!claudeExecutable): it needs Claude Code on PATH, which a hosted macOS runner does not have, so requiring it would fail every hosted run. It still runs on a developer Mac with claude on PATH.

test: Seatbelt profile under the real kernel
the installed Claude Code answers its handshake inside the restricted profile, and its model request reaches the model endpoint only through the broker
notRequired.reason: Guarded by test.skipIf(!claudeExecutable): it needs Claude Code on PATH, which a hosted macOS runner does not have, so requiring it would fail every hosted run. It still runs on a developer Mac with claude on PATH.

linux-bubblewrap-kernel.description: Kernel legs of the Linux bubblewrap confinement sandbox (#4770, #4772). They run only on a Linux host where bwrap applies the production sandbox (unprivileged user namespaces allowed), and are skipped elsewhere. The live Claude handshake uses `claude` on PATH or the Agent SDK's own binary for the platform, which dependencies:ci installs, so it is required too.

test: bubblewrap sandbox under the real kernel
a nested user namespace cannot be created inside, so the mounts cannot be rearranged
mayRuntimeSkip.reason: Skips at runtime (ctx.skip) when `unshare --user` cannot create a user namespace even outside the sandbox (util-linux missing, or a host policy), so the refusal inside would prove nothing. A skip is recorded, a failure is not accepted.

test: bubblewrap sandbox under the real kernel
the host's Docker socket refuses a connection from inside
mayRuntimeSkip.reason: Skips at runtime (ctx.skip) when no Docker socket exists that this user can connect to outside the sandbox, so the refusal inside would prove nothing. A hosted runner whose user is in the docker group runs it; a skip is recorded, a failure is not accepted. The hidden-socket leg proves the mechanism on every host.

test: bubblewrap sandbox under the real kernel
a name resolves through DNS inside the sandbox
mayRuntimeSkip.reason: Skips at runtime (ctx.skip) when this host cannot resolve a name outside the sandbox either (no resolver or no network), so a failure inside would prove nothing. A skip is recorded, a failure is not accepted.
